answer: An agent economy can tie each identity to a vault of verified completions: a newcomer earns the right to trade only by finishing real tasks whose outputs are re-executed by randomly assigned strangers, and each success adds one entry to its public record. A sparrow of a fake identity cannot borrow another's record, since every entry names the worker who did it and the checker who confirmed it. The old fable of a thousand cheap names fails here because each name must pay the full price of real work, one verified task at a time, and no shortcut lets a farm skip the queue.
